inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report: equity-settled share-based compensation US$14,534k (the same figure added back in the company's adjusted EBITDA/adjusted net profit reconciliation). No net-share-settlement tax line: RSUs are satisfied from trustee-held or newly issued shares, no withholding outflow appears in financing. H1 FY2026 SBC jumped to US$16,984k (1.5% of revenue) after the 12 June 2026 grant of 62,966,166 new-share RSUs.
inputs.fx_note: USD -> HKD at 7.8479 (Yahoo Finance HKD=X chart API, regularMarketTime 2026-10-16). Inside the HKMA 7.75-7.85 link band, so direction is unambiguous: HK$ value = US$ value x 7.8479 (fx_rate converts model currency to quote currency). Parity checks (no US dual listing exists): (1) Temasek's US$150m for ~90.5m shares = US$1.657/share x 7.8479 = HK$13.00, against the HK$12.99 average entry price reported for the stake; (2) H1 FY2026 diluted EPS US 2.77 cents annualised = US 5.54 cents = HK 43.5 cents, giving ~25x at the HKEX close, consistent with the stock's quoted trailing P/E in the mid-20s.

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted 1,745.8m = 1,684.58m shares in issue at 30 June 2026 (interim report substantial-shareholder note, includes the 47.46m convertible-bond conversion shares allotted 2 June 2026 and ~107m shares held by RSU trustees, all counted as outstanding) + ~61.2m new shares issuable for RSUs granted under the scheme mandate (3.98% of the 1,537.55m weighted average, per the interim report). The convertible bond is fully converted, no share options outstanding. Held FLAT because SBC is expensed in the flows. Temasek's ~5.7% stake (May 2026) was bought from existing holders -- no share-issue proceeds appear in the H1 FY2026 financing cash flow -- so it adds no shares. Post-period buybacks (HK$300m programme approved July 2026; HK$3-68m per month Jul-Sep at HK$9.6-14) are not deducted because the cancellation count is not yet in a filing; this is conservative by roughly 1%.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Flows are USD, so WACC is USD-built: US 10y risk-free ~4.3% + beta ~1.25 x 5.0% ERP = ~10.5% cost of equity, plus nothing for debt (no interest-bearing borrowings at 30 June 2026 bar a US$15.2m overdraft). 10.5% matches the house USD tech default and is held identical across all three scenarios -- China-rooted regulatory, gaming-concentration and competitive risk are charged in the bear flows and the 25% bear weight, not in a stacked premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: lease liabilities of US$7.43m (2.671 current + 4.754 non-current) sit in total_debt; lease principal (US$1.4m in H1 FY2026) is NOT deducted from flows. Ongoing office-lease renewal is charged through lease_cost_pct_path at 0.1% of revenue (~US$2.5-5m/yr, in line with the ~US$3m/yr cash lease cost). Immaterial either way.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI stock of US$7.07m deducted once in the equity bridge; profit attributable to NCI was nil in FY2025 and H1 FY2026, so the flows need no leakage driver.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF (component build, 10-year horizon), routed from SKILL.md as an operating company (programmatic ad-tech platform) with the non-US adaptations applied for dual currency (USD statements, HKD quote) and leases. First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry. Revenue is reported GROSS of publisher traffic cost, so margins are thin by construction (adjusted EBITDA 9.3% FY2025, 8.3% H1 FY2026); the margin paths are on gross revenue and must not be compared with net-revenue peers like AppLovin. Adjusted EBITDA (company definition, excludes SBC and FVPL fair-value changes) is the ebitda_margin anchor: FY2025 US$190.9m / US$2,046.7m = 9.3%. Capex = capitalised development costs + PP&E (FY2025 US$54.3m, 2.65%; H1 FY2026 US$39.4m, 3.4% as AI-Infra development ramps). Cash tax FY2025 US$11.7m on EBIT of ~US$103m (~11%), ramped to 18% (Singapore 17%, China HNTE 15%, Pillar Two 15% floor). Working capital: trade payables (US$407m) + contract liabilities (US$63m) exceed receivables (US$313m) + prepayments (US$63m), so growth releases cash -- FY2025 OCF exceeded adjusted EBITDA less tax by ~US$35m on +US$539m revenue (~6.5%); capture set at 5% of the revenue increase (3% bear). Cash = US$193.4m cash and equivalents + US$46.7m money-market funds held at FVPL (current) = US$240.1m; restricted cash US$5.4m (pledged) excluded. Interest income is stripped from last_fcf because net cash (US$217m) exceeds the owner-FCF base. Non-operating FVPL assets (unlisted exchangeable bonds US$65.6m + others US$10.95m) go in the equity bridge at a 25% illiquidity haircut because their fair-value gains (US$11.6m in H1 FY2026) are excluded from adjusted EBITDA (matching-asset rule). Buybacks: none in FY2025 (US$0); FY2024 US$6.2m; a HK$300m programme started July 2026, so the flat count is now partly funded by repurchases.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (7.1% 3yr, 1.6% 5yr) diverges by far more than 30% from revenue (31.7-31.8%) and EPS (58.7% 3yr off a US 1.0c base). Equity is distorted by the FY2021-22 Reyun write-downs, buybacks and the 2026 convertible conversion, and the 31.7% revenue CAGR is a gross-basis figure now decelerating (H1 FY2026 +23.2% vs FY2025 +35.7%), so neither is used. Selected rate is the base case's own 10-year revenue CAGR (19% decelerating to 4%).
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - interest income), US$m: FY2020 -35.7, FY2021 -24.4, FY2022 4.4, FY2023 18.1, FY2024 206.5, FY2025 140.7. The 3yr owner-FCF CAGR (218%) compounds off a near-zero FY2022 base and is meaningless; FY2024 was flattered by a ~US$150m working-capital release. 5yr FCF and EPS CAGRs are undefined (negative FY2020 start). Owner-FCF growth is NOT lagging reported-FCF growth because SBC was falling as a share of revenue through FY2025 -- but H1 FY2026 SBC quadrupled to 1.5% of revenue on the June 2026 mega-grant, so that tailwind has reversed.

base.narrative: FY2026 lands ~+19% (H1 +23.2%, H2 decelerating off a tougher comp); growth fades to 4% by year 10 as smart bidding saturates Mintegral. Adjusted EBITDA margin dips to 8.6% in FY2026 on AI-Infra server cost, then recovers to 10.5% on operating leverage.

scenario_narratives.base: Smart bidding (now >90% of Mintegral revenue) keeps taking share of medium-and-long-tail mobile app supply, non-gaming verticals (e-commerce, short drama, AI apps, ~25% of Mintegral) keep growing faster than gaming, and the October 2026 AI-Infra rollout pays for its server cost through better delivery efficiency rather than expanding margins outright. Revenue grows ~19% in FY2026 and fades to 4% by FY2035 (10% ten-year CAGR, roughly the mobile-ad market's ~10% CAGR plus a little share gain early). Adjusted EBITDA margin on gross revenue recovers from 8.3% (H1 FY2026) to 10.5% as sales, G&A and R&D ratios fall with scale. SBC stays elevated at ~1.4% of revenue while the June 2026 RSU grant vests, then eases to 0.9%.
scenario_narratives.bull: The IAP ROAS inflection sell-side flags for Q4 2026 lands: Mintegral breaks into midcore/hardcore games and IAP-heavy advertisers, non-gaming becomes a second engine, and the independent-network position strengthens as developers diversify away from AppLovin's pricing. Growth stays above 20% for two years and fades only to 4% by year 10; AI-Infra lifts algorithm efficiency so adjusted EBITDA margin climbs to 13% on gross revenue (take rate and server-cost ratio both improve). Terminal growth 3.5% reflects a structurally larger in-app-advertising market.
scenario_narratives.bear: H1 FY2026's deceleration (+23% after +36%) is the start of a fade, not a pause: AppLovin, Pangle and Google AdMob out-invest Mintegral on AI bidding with first-party data, hyper-casual fatigue spreads through its ~75% gaming book, and a privacy shock (Google Privacy Sandbox on Android or a further ATT-style tightening) or China-linked cross-border data scrutiny impairs targeting. Growth drops to 8% in FY2027 and low single digits thereafter; the AI-Infra spend becomes a permanent cost, compressing adjusted EBITDA margin to 7% on gross revenue, and the working-capital float grows more slowly.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: Mobvista is a thin-margin intermediary with no owned audience, competing against walled gardens and AppLovin that can out-invest it, with ~75% gaming concentration and regulatory exposure on two fronts (Western privacy regimes, China data rules), and growth has already started decelerating. Base 50% is the decelerating-but-profitable path the H1 FY2026 data supports. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right at once (IAP inflection, non-gaming scaling, AI-Infra margin payback).

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on gross-basis revenue with SBC fully expensed and the share count held flat at the fully diluted 1,745.8m. Values computed in USD and converted to HKD at 7.8479 for comparison with the HKEX price. The thesis is a decelerating but cash-generative independent ad network whose negative working capital funds its own growth; most of the value sits in the terminal years, so the margin path on gross revenue (8.6% -> 10.5% base) is the decisive lever.
key_risks_to_valuation: Adjusted EBITDA margin on GROSS revenue: each 1pp of terminal margin is worth roughly 10-15% of value; a shift to more net-basis revenue recognition would rescale every margin
Growth deceleration: H1 FY2026 +23.2% vs FY2025 +35.7%; base assumes ~19% for FY2026
Competition from AppLovin, Pangle, Google AdMob and Unity on AI bidding with first-party data
Privacy/regulatory shocks (Android Privacy Sandbox, ATT-style changes, China cross-border data rules)
SBC re-acceleration: H1 FY2026 SBC 1.5% of revenue after the 63m-share June 2026 grant; base holds ~1.4% for two years
Valuation of the unlisted exchangeable bonds (US$65.6m at fair value, carried at a 25% haircut)
FX rate in fx_rate is not refreshed by price-only updates; the HKD peg keeps drift small
